title: Bharat Ratna — India's Highest Civilian Honour
answer: The Bharat Ratna is the highest civilian award of the Republic of India, instituted on 2 January 1954. The first recipients in 1954 were C. Rajagopalachari, Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, and Dr. C.V. Raman.
highlights: First Recipients (1954): C. Rajagopalachari (last Governor-General), Dr. S. Radhakrishnan (philosopher & 1st Vice President), Dr. C.V. Raman (Nobel physicist)
Non-Indian Awardees: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan (Frontier Gandhi, 1987) and Nelson Mandela (1990)
Youngest Recipient: Sachin Tendulkar (awarded in 2014 at age 40, first and only sportsperson)
2024 Conferments: Karpoori Thakur, Lal Krishna Advani, P.V. Narasimha Rao, Chaudhary Charan Singh, and Dr. M.S. Swaminathan

title: Indian Nobel Prize Laureates (1913 – Present)
answer: Rabindranath Tagore was the first Indian (and first Asian) to win the Nobel Prize, receiving the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913 for 'Gitanjali'. Other Indian Nobel laureates include C.V. Raman (Physics 1930), Mother Teresa (Peace 1979), Amartya Sen (Economics 1998), and Kailash Satyarthi (Peace 2014).
highlights: Rabindranath Tagore (1913, Literature): First Asian Nobel laureate for 'Gitanjali'
Sir C.V. Raman (1930, Physics): For the discovery of the Raman Effect (scattering of light)
Mother Teresa (1979, Peace): For humanitarian service to the poor and destitute in Kolkata
Amartya Sen (1998, Economics): For welfare economics and poverty/famine analysis
Kailash Satyarthi (2014, Peace): For child rights advocacy (Bachpan Bachao Andolan)
Indian-Origin Laureates: Har Gobind Khorana (Medicine 1968), Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar (Physics 1983), Venkatraman Ramakrishnan (Chemistry 2009), Abhijit Banerjee (Economics 2019)

title: Padma Awards Hierarchy (Vibhushan, Bhushan & Shri)
answer: The Padma Awards are India's second, third, and fourth highest civilian honours announced annually on the eve of Republic Day (25 January). The descending hierarchy is: Bharat Ratna (1st) → Padma Vibhushan (for exceptional and distinguished service) → Padma Bhushan (distinguished service of a high order) → Padma Shri (distinguished service).
highlights: Padma Vibhushan: 2nd highest civilian award (exceptional and distinguished service in any field)
Padma Bhushan: 3rd highest civilian award (distinguished service of high order)
Padma Shri: 4th highest civilian award (distinguished service in arts, education, industry, literature, science, sports, social service)
Institution: Established in 1954; presented by the President of India at Rashtrapati Bhavan

title: Indian Academy Award (Oscar) Winners
answer: Bhanu Athaiya was the first Indian to win an Oscar, winning Best Costume Design in 1983 for Richard Attenborough's film 'Gandhi'. At the 95th Academy Awards in 2023, 'Naatu Naatu' from the film 'RRR' won Best Original Song, and 'The Elephant Whisperers' won Best Documentary Short.

title: Jnanpith Award — India's Highest Literary Honour
answer: The Jnanpith Award is India's highest and oldest literary award, instituted in 1961 by the Bharatiya Jnanpith. The first recipient in 1965 was Malayalam poet G. Sankara Kurup for his anthology 'Odakkuzhal' (The Bamboo Flute). Ashapoorna Devi was the first woman to win the award in 1976 for her Bengali novel 'Pratham Pratishruti'.
highlights: First Recipient (1965): G. Sankara Kurup (Malayalam literature for 'Odakkuzhal')
First Woman Recipient (1976): Ashapoorna Devi (Bengali literature for 'Pratham Pratishruti')
First English Awardee (2018): Amitav Ghosh
Conferment: Bronze replica of Goddess Saraswati (Vagdevi) and cash prize of ₹11 lakh

answer: The Dadasaheb Phalke Award is India's highest award in the field of cinema, presented annually at the National Film Awards ceremony by the Directorate of Film Festivals. First awarded in 1969 to actress Devika Rani (the 'First Lady of Indian Cinema'), it commemorates Dadasaheb Phalke, who directed India's first full-length feature film 'Raja Harishchandra' (1913).

answer: Key globally recognized international days include International Women's Day (8 March), World Health Day (7 April — WHO foundation), Earth Day (22 April), and World Environment Day (5 June — UN Stockholm Conference 1972).

title: Indian Parliament Seats — Lok Sabha (543) & Rajya Sabha (250)
answer: The Lok Sabha currently has 543 directly elected Members of Parliament (MPs) across territorial constituencies. The Rajya Sabha has a maximum strength of 250 members (238 elected by State/UT Legislative Assemblies and 12 nominated by the President of India for expertise in literature, science, art, and social service).

Rajya Sabha (250 Seats): 238 representatives of States/UTs + 12 Presidential Nominees (UP has highest with 31 seats)

answer: The official national symbols of India include the Royal Bengal Tiger (National Animal), Indian Peacock (National Bird), Lotus (National Flower), Banyan Tree (National Tree), Mango (National Fruit), Ganga (National River), and Ganges River Dolphin (National Aquatic Animal).

National Heritage Animal: Indian Elephant (Elephas maximus indicus — declared in 2010)

title: National Anthem, National Song & Indian Rupee Symbol (₹)
answer: India's National Anthem is 'Jana Gana Mana', composed in Bengali by Rabindranath Tagore, with an official full singing duration of 52 seconds. The National Song is 'Vande Mataram', composed in Sanskrit by Bankim Chandra Chatterjee in his novel 'Anandamath'. The official Indian Rupee currency symbol (₹) was designed by D. Udaya Kumar and adopted by the Government of India on 15 July 2010.

National Song: 'Vande Mataram' (Composed by Bankim Chandra Chatterjee in 1870s; first sung at 1896 Congress session by Rabindranath Tagore)

Indian Rupee Symbol (₹): Designed by D. Udaya Kumar (IIT Bombay / IIT Guwahati professor); combines Devanagari 'र' (Ra) and Roman capital 'R' with two parallel horizontal stripes representing the tricolour flag and economic equality

title: ISRO Landmark Space Missions (Chandrayaan, Mangalyaan & Gaganyaan)
answer: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) was founded on 15 August 1969 by Dr. Vikram Sarabhai ('Father of Indian Space Programme') with headquarters in Bengaluru. On 23 August 2023, Chandrayaan-3 achieved historical success by making India the first country in the world to softly land near the Moon's South Pole (landing site named 'Shiv Shakti Point', celebrated as National Space Day).
highlights: Chandrayaan-3: Landed Vikram lander and Pragyan rover near lunar south pole on 23 August 2023 (making India the 4th country to land on Moon, and 1st near South Pole)
Mangalyaan (Mars Orbiter Mission / MOM): Launched 5 November 2013; entered Martian orbit on 24 September 2014 on India's maiden attempt at lowest global cost (~$74M)
Aryabhata: India's first satellite, launched on 19 April 1975 using a Soviet Kosmos-3M launch vehicle
Gaganyaan: India's indigenous human spaceflight mission designed to carry a crew of 3 astronauts to Low Earth Orbit (LEO)
Launch Vehicles: PSLV (Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle - 'Workhorse of ISRO'), GSLV Mk III / LVM3

title: James Webb Space Telescope (JWST)
answer: The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) is the premier space observatory developed by NASA, ESA, and CSA, launched on 25 December 2021. Positioned in a halo orbit around the Sun-Earth Lagrange point L2 (~1.5 million km from Earth), its 6.5-metre gold-coated beryllium mirror conducts ultra-deep infrared observations of the earliest galaxies formed after the Big Bang.
highlights: Launch: 25 December 2021 aboard an Ariane 5 rocket from Kourou, French Guiana
Orbit: Sun-Earth Lagrange Point L2 (1.5 million km / 1 million miles from Earth)
Primary Mirror: 6.5 metres (21.3 ft) in diameter composed of 18 hexagonal gold-plated beryllium segments
Primary Mission: High-resolution infrared imaging of early universe star formation, exoplanet atmospheric spectroscopy, and galaxy evolution

title: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) — Central Bank of India
answer: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is India's central bank and regulatory body for the banking system, established on 1 April 1935 under the Reserve Bank of India Act 1934 based on the Hilton Young Commission recommendations. Sir Osborne Smith was its first Governor, and C.D. Deshmukh was the first Indian Governor.
highlights: Establishment: 1 April 1935 in Kolkata (moved permanently to Mumbai in 1937); nationalized on 1 January 1949
Key Governors: Sir Osborne Smith (1st Governor, 1935–1937), C.D. Deshmukh (1st Indian Governor, 1943–1949), Dr. Manmohan Singh (Governor 1982–1985)
Key Monetary Policy Rates: Repo Rate (rate at which RBI lends short-term money to commercial banks), Reverse Repo Rate, Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR), Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)
Core Functions: Sole authority to issue currency banknotes (except ₹1 note/coins issued by Ministry of Finance), banker to government and banks, lender of last resort, forex reserve manager

title: Indian Stock Exchanges: BSE (Sensex) & NSE (Nifty 50)
answer: The Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE), founded by Premchand Roychand in 1875 on Dalal Street (Mumbai), is Asia's oldest stock exchange with its benchmark index being the S&P BSE SENSEX (30 blue-chip stocks). The National Stock Exchange (NSE), established in 1992, is India's largest financial exchange with its flagship index being the NIFTY 50.
highlights: BSE (Bombay Stock Exchange): Founded 9 July 1875 (Native Share & Stock Brokers' Association); Asia's first stock exchange; benchmark index SENSEX (Base year: 1978–79 = 100)
NSE (National Stock Exchange): Established 1992; pioneered fully automated screen-based electronic trading in India; benchmark index NIFTY 50 (Base year: 1995 = 1000)
Regulator: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI, established 1988, statutory powers under SEBI Act 1992)

title: NITI Aayog — Think Tank of the Government of India
answer: NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) is the premier public policy think tank of the Government of India, established on 1 January 2015 by the Union Cabinet to replace the 65-year-old Soviet-style Planning Commission. The Prime Minister of India serves as its ex-officio Chairperson.
highlights: Full Form: National Institution for Transforming India
Founded: 1 January 2015 (replaced the Planning Commission established in 1950)
Leadership: Chairperson (Prime Minister of India), Vice-Chairperson, Chief Executive Officer (CEO), and Governing Council comprising all State Chief Ministers and UT Lt. Governors
Key Philosophy: Cooperative federalism, bottom-up approach, sustainable development goals (SDG India Index), Atal Innovation Mission (AIM)

title: Goods and Services Tax (GST) in India
answer: The Goods and Services Tax (GST) is a comprehensive, multi-stage, destination-based indirect tax levied on the supply of goods and services across India, implemented on 1 July 2017 via the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act under the motto 'One Nation, One Tax, One Market'.
highlights: Launch Date: 1 July 2017 (Midnight session of Parliament)
Constitutional Backing: 101st Constitutional Amendment Act 2016 (Article 279A creates GST Council chaired by Union Finance Minister)
Four Primary Tax Slabs: 5%, 12%, 18%, and 28% (essential items/food grains at 0%; precious metals like gold at special 3%)
Three Types of GST: CGST (Central GST collected by Center), SGST/UTGST (State/UT GST collected by States), and IGST (Integrated GST on inter-state trade and imports collected by Center and shared)

title: India's Economy Size & Global GDP Ranking
answer: India is the world's 5th largest economy by nominal Gross Domestic Product (GDP) with an economic output exceeding $3.9 Trillion (surpassing the United Kingdom in 2022) and the 3rd largest economy in the world by Purchasing Power Parity (PPP) behind China and the United States.
highlights: Nominal GDP Rank: 5th largest in the world (behind USA, China, Germany, Japan)
PPP (Purchasing Power Parity) Rank: 3rd largest in the world (~$14+ Trillion PPP)
Economic Sectors: Services sector (~54% of GVA), Industry/Manufacturing (~28%), Agriculture & Allied (~18% of GVA while employing ~45% of workforce)
Growth Rate: Fastest-growing major global economy among G20 nations

answer: Neeraj Chopra is an Indian track and field athlete who won the Gold Medal in Men's Javelin Throw at the 2020 Tokyo Olympics with an 87.58-metre throw on 7 August 2021, becoming the first Indian track and field athlete in history to win an Olympic gold medal.

title: Major Dhyan Chand — 'The Wizard of Hockey'
answer: Major Dhyan Chand (29 August 1905 – 3 December 1979) was an Indian field hockey player widely regarded as the greatest hockey player in sports history. He led the Indian hockey team to three consecutive Olympic Gold Medals in 1928 (Amsterdam), 1932 (Los Angeles), and 1936 (Berlin).
highlights: Three Olympic Golds: 1928 Amsterdam, 1932 Los Angeles, 1936 Berlin (where he scored over 400 international goals in his career)
Birthday Commemoration: 29 August is celebrated annually as India's National Sports Day (Rashtriya Khel Diwas)
Renamed Honour: India's highest sporting award, formerly Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna, was officially renamed the 'Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award' in 2021

answer: Mithali Raj is an Indian former cricketer and captain who is the all-time highest run-scorer in women's international cricket with over 10,000 international runs across formats (7,805 runs in ODIs alone). She led India to two ICC Women's Cricket World Cup finals (2005 and 2017).

Longevity: International career spanning 23 years (1999–2022), appearing in 6 ICC Women's World Cups
National Honors: Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna (2021), Padma Shri (2015), Arjuna Award (2003)

title: Sania Mirza — India's Most Successful Female Tennis Player
answer: Sania Mirza is a former professional Indian tennis player who won 6 Grand Slam titles (3 in Women's Doubles and 3 in Mixed Doubles) and was ranked World No. 1 in Women's Doubles by the WTA for 91 weeks. World No. 1: Held WTA World No. 1 doubles ranking for 91 consecutive weeks

title: New 7 Wonders of the World
answer: The New 7 Wonders of the World (chosen by global poll in 2007) are: (1) Great Wall of China, (2) Petra (Jordan), (3) Colosseum (Rome, Italy), (4) Chichén Itzá (Mexico), (5) Machu Picchu (Peru), (6) Taj Mahal (Agra, India), and (7) Christ the Redeemer (Rio de Janeiro, Brazil). Machu Picchu: 15th-century Inca citadel on mountain ridge in Andes, Peru (2,430 m above sea level)

title: The Nobel Prize — History, Categories & Records
answer: The Nobel Prize was established in 1895 by the will of Swedish chemist and dynamite inventor Alfred Nobel. Prizes are awarded annually in 6 categories: Physics, Chemistry, Physiology or Medicine, Literature, Peace, and Economic Sciences (established 1968 by Sveriges Riksbank). Nobel Peace Prize is awarded in Oslo, Norway; all other 5 prizes are presented in Stockholm, Sweden on 10 December (Nobel's death anniversary).
highlights: First awarded: 10 December 1901 (Wilhelm Röntgen won first Physics Nobel for discovering X-rays)

title: Solar System — Order of Planets and Key Facts
answer: The Solar System has 8 official planets ordered by distance from the Sun: Mercury (closest, smallest), Venus (hottest ~465°C, brightest, rotates clockwise), Earth (only known life), Mars (Red Planet, Olympus Mons volcano), Jupiter (largest, Great Red Spot, 95 moons), Saturn (prominent ring system, Titan moon), Uranus (ice giant, rotates on its side at 98° tilt), and Neptune (farthest, fastest winds ~2,100 km/h). Pluto was reclassified as a Dwarf Planet by the IAU in August 2006.
highlights: Inner/Terrestrial planets (rocky): Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars | Outer/Jovian planets (gas/ice giants): Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune
Hottest planet: Venus (~465°C due to dense 96% CO₂ runaway greenhouse atmosphere)
Largest planet & moon: Jupiter is largest planet; Ganymede (Jupiter's moon) is largest moon in solar system (bigger than Mercury)
Tallest volcano: Olympus Mons on Mars (22 km high — nearly 3 times height of Mt. Everest)
Asteroid belt lies between Mars and Jupiter; Kuiper belt lies beyond Neptune
